identity.canonicalName: Zara Home Semi-Sphere Table Lamp, Silver

classification.verdictNote: Zara Home's own design, sold only by Zara and Zara Home. It echoes 1970s Italian chrome eyeball lamps.
classification.summary: An original Zara Home product with no credited designer, sold only through Zara Home and Zara. The polished steel sphere with a cut-away face recalls 1960s and 1970s Italian space-age lamps, such as Goffredo Reggiani's chrome eyeball lamps, which trade as collectible vintage. It isn't a copy of a specific current product.

quality: A small accent lamp rather than a reading light: a polished steel ball with the face cut away, so the bulb glows from inside a black cup. It throws light in one direction, which makes it good for a shelf, console or floor corner.
Polished steel shows fingerprints and the finish can scratch. For the look's original, search vintage "Reggiani eyeball lamp" on 1stDibs or Pamono, where period pieces cost many times more.

maker.name: Zara Home
paragraphs: Zara Home is the home decor chain of Inditex, the Spanish group behind Zara. It launched in August 2003, is based in A Coruña, Spain, and sells bedding, tableware, furniture and decor through its own stores and website.
Like Zara, it follows fast-moving trends with frequent new collections and doesn't credit individual designers on most pieces. The same lamp also appears on zara.com.

items.name: Goffredo Reggiani eyeball lamps (1960s to 1970s)
items.priceNote: Vintage pieces from about £230 (around $300) on Vinterior; more on 1stDibs
items.why: The chrome sphere with a cut-away face that Zara's lamp echoes. Real Reggiani pieces are adjustable and made in Italy, but vintage condition varies, so check the wiring and chrome.

similar.note: Few new lamps share this exact shape. The reverse image search mostly returned Zara's own lamp, vintage Italian originals and props.
